chapter: Leo Watson and the Panassie sessions
title: What he recalls of the Panassie session and meeting Hugues Panassie
summary: He cannot remember the day or tunes, but players were often up all night before record dates; Panassie was wonderful to him.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yeah, right. Well, thinking about all these guys, can you remember the session at all?
No, I don't.
Uh-huh.
Don't remember what day it was, or you know --
Well, some people have said that a lot of the guys were hungover.
Well, they could have been, because we'd make them certain days that them guys would stay up all night long. That was the habit around there.
Yeah.
It was the habit of staying up all night and then getting up and trying to make a record date.
It was nothing unusual.
No.
Yeah. How was your feeling towards Panassié?
Well, Hugues Panassié was a very wonderful person to me.
Uh-huh. Where did you first meet him?
Oh, I met Hugues Panassié in New York.
In New York.
Yeah.
At an earlier time?
Oh, it was about a couple of years before I seen him and got to know him well.
I see. I see. Do you remember if he requested any particular tunes on that session?
Hugues?
Yeah. The whole session was his project, I guess.
Yeah.
Do you remember anything about the tunes that were called, or --
No, I don't remember the tunes that were called because it's been so long.
